# Final claim–evidence map

**Generated by `export_claim_evidence_map.py` from the authoritative tables.**
Machine-readable form: `outputs/tables/final_claim_evidence.csv` (16 columns,
13 claims). Numeric fields are read from the generator CSVs, never typed, so
this map cannot drift from the tables.

Read this before writing any sentence of the manuscript. Each claim carries
**allowed wording** and **forbidden stronger wording**. The forbidden column is
not stylistic: each entry is a specific over-claim the evidence does not support.

## Inferential vocabulary

| instrument | role |
|---|---|
| crossed seed × case bootstrap | uncertainty interval — **not** a test |
| paired seed-level *t*-test | formal inferential test |
| Holm | multiplicity adjustment, across the two interaction tests only |
| exact sign-flip | distribution-free sensitivity analysis (floor 0.0625 at n=5) |
| seed SD, sign count | descriptive stability diagnostics |

An effect with adjusted *p* < 0.05 **and** an interval excluding zero is
**"statistically supported under the study's inferential framework"**. The
phrase "two-bar rule" is retired and must not appear.

## P1 — PRIMARY

> Moving from frozen linear probing to matched full fine-tuning changes the
> relative QWK difference between ImageNet-MAE and RETFound.

| | DDR | APTOS |
|---|---|---|
| interaction I_full | **−0.1141** | **−0.0992** |
| crossed 95% CI | [−0.1548, −0.0728] | [−0.1595, −0.0397] |
| raw paired seed *p* | 0.0066 | 0.0370 |
| **Holm-adjusted *p*** | **0.0132** | **0.0370** |
| sign agreement | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| n test | 12,424 | 3,504 |

Source: `JBHI_PRIMARY_INTERACTION.csv`. Seeds 42, 1, 2, 3, 4, paired within
seed. **Supported on both domains.**

**ALLOWED**
- "The large frozen-probe ImageNet-MAE advantage was substantially attenuated
  under matched full fine-tuning on both held-out domains."
- "The protocol-by-initialization interaction was statistically supported on
  both domains under the final two-domain Holm-adjusted analysis."

**FORBIDDEN**
- "RETFound is superior under full fine-tuning."
- "The models are equivalent after fine-tuning."
- "Linear probing reverses the ranking on every domain."
- "This behaviour generalizes to all retinal foundation models."

## S1 — SECONDARY: model comparison under full fine-tuning

| | DDR | APTOS |
|---|---|---|
| Δ (ImageNet-MAE − RETFound) | −0.0439 | +0.0083 |
| crossed 95% CI | [−0.0861, −0.0103] | [−0.0095, +0.0258] |
| paired seed *p* | 0.1035 | 0.3489 |
| sign agreement | 4/5 | 4/5 |
| status | **not demonstrated** | **not demonstrated** |

Source: `JBHI_MASTER_RESULTS.csv`.

**Note the DDR disagreement.** Its crossed interval excludes zero while the
formal seed-level test does not reject. Under this study's framework the formal
test governs, so **no difference is claimed on DDR**. The disagreement is
informative — the effect is consistent across *patients* but not across *seeds*
— and should be reported as such rather than resolved in favour of the interval.

**ALLOWED**
- "No difference between the two initialisations was demonstrated under matched
  full fine-tuning on either domain."
- For DDR: "the crossed uncertainty interval excludes zero while the formal
  seed-level test does not reject; under the study's framework no difference is
  claimed."

**FORBIDDEN**
- "The two initialisations are equivalent."
- "RETFound matches ImageNet-MAE after fine-tuning."
- "RETFound outperforms ImageNet-MAE on DDR." (mean favours RETFound; the test
  does not support it)
- "Full fine-tuning eliminates the difference."

## S2 — SECONDARY: exploratory metrics

Macro AUROC (+0.0241, *p* = 0.0394) and ECE (−0.0126, *p* = 0.0246) favour
ImageNet-MAE on APTOS at uncorrected *p* < 0.05. Source:
`aptos_secondary_outcomes.csv`.

**Neither is claimed.** Nine-metric exploratory set, uncorrected; roughly one
such value is expected by chance. QWK is the pre-specified endpoint and shows no
difference.

**FORBIDDEN**: "ImageNet-MAE is better calibrated", "significantly higher
AUROC", "secondary metrics confirm the advantage".

## D1/D2 — DESCRIPTIVE: frozen probing is not uniform across domains

| held out | Δ frozen (ten seeds) | crossed 95% CI | favours |
|---|---|---|---|
| DDR | +0.0626 | [+0.0440, +0.0824] | ImageNet-MAE |
| APTOS | +0.1134 | [+0.0787, +0.1493] | ImageNet-MAE |
| **IDRiD** | **−0.0429** | [−0.0888, +0.0037] | **RETFound** |

Source: `JBHI_MASTER_RESULTS.csv`, `seed_set = all-10`.

**This matters for framing.** The frozen-probe advantage is *not* a universal
ImageNet-MAE advantage: IDRiD reverses its direction. Any sentence implying
"frozen probing favours ImageNet-MAE" must be qualified by domain.

**FORBIDDEN**: "Frozen probing consistently favours ImageNet-MAE", or
differencing a ten-seed frozen estimate against a five-seed adaptation estimate.

## D3 — DESCRIPTIVE: optimisation behaviour

Across DDR + APTOS full fine-tuning, source validation only:

| | ImageNet-MAE | RETFound |
|---|---|---|
| early stopped | **0/10** | **10/10** |
| best epoch (DDR / APTOS) | 17.6 ± 1.5 / 18.0 ± 1.0 | 8.6 ± 1.7 / 9.2 ± 2.6 |
| overfit ratio | 1.10 ± 0.05 / 1.14 ± 0.02 | 2.39 ± 0.36 / 2.50 ± 0.32 |

**ALLOWED**: reported as mechanistic *context*.
**FORBIDDEN**: "Overfitting causes the interaction", "the budget disadvantaged
RETFound", any causal or visual causal claim.

## Language rule: attenuation, not reversal

| domain | frozen | partial | full | mean ordering |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| APTOS | +0.1075 | +0.0073 | +0.0083 | ImageNet-MAE ahead **at every depth** |
| DDR | +0.0702 | +0.0217 | −0.0439 | crosses zero at full FT |

On **APTOS the mean ordering never reverses** — only the magnitude collapses.
Therefore:

- **Preferred:** "The magnitude of the apparent ImageNet-MAE advantage under
  frozen probing is strongly attenuated when the encoder is allowed to adapt."
- **Do not write:** "the ranking reverses" or "the ranking does not survive" as
  a general two-domain conclusion.
- A numerical mean reversal **on DDR** may be described descriptively, and must
  not be generalised to APTOS.

---

## L1–L4 — LIMITATIONS that must appear

| id | limitation |
|---|---|
| **L1** | IDRiD contributes **no** full fine-tuning evidence. The interaction is a two-domain result. No IDRiD full-FT value is imputed anywhere. |
| **L2** | The two-domain family is a **post-hoc pairing**: DDR was observed before APTOS was specified. APTOS's recipe and analysis were frozen before any APTOS target outcome was inspected, and Holm is applied for conservative final reporting — but this is **not** a prospectively specified two-domain design. |
| **L3** | EyePACS is in RETFound's published pretraining corpus and is a **source** domain here. No held-out target image was seen in pretraining or training; the exposure applies identically to both protocol arms and cannot generate the interaction. **Do not call this target leakage.** |
| **L4** | **Demographic subgroup fairness could not be evaluated.** Verified 2026-09-12 by inspecting the label files of all four releases: the only columns present are image identifiers, DR grade, macular-oedema risk and lesion coordinates. **No age, sex, race or ethnicity field exists in any release.** Mandated sentence: *"Demographic subgroup fairness could not be evaluated because harmonized patient demographic attributes were not available across the public releases."* Do not infer demographics from images; do not report any subgroup analysis. |

Further scope limits for the Discussion: two initialisations, one architecture
(ViT-L/16), one adaptation budget, five seeds per protocol, QWK as the primary
endpoint, and runs that are not bit-reproducible by design.
